advances:
The transverse needle lemma in the exact centroidal-triangle stratum holds
with a stronger constant than the proposed \(4/9\):
\[
\limsup\frac{|P_\varnothing|}{|K|}
\le \frac{392}{911}<\frac49.
\]
The proof retains all four relative \(Q\)-cell masses.  The third
\(Q\)-halfspace is used before taking the one-dimensional limit: its good
part is a convex body of relative area \(31/36\), and the other two
\(Q\)-caps are equal tails of relative mass \(5/31\) inside that body.
An exact equal-tail lemma for concave densities forces their combined
projection width to be at least \(10/31\).  Reflected thresholds and
midpoint containment then reduce \(P_\varnothing\) to an explicit
three-variable box slice, whose area is at most \(392/911\) of the
centroidal triangle.

This packet treats the exact centroidal-triangle needle stratum only.  It
does not assert a quantitative stability transfer to near-triangular middle
bodies.
author: /root/mp_r55_escape_sections
proof:
We first prove the one-dimensional fact that will retain the third
\(Q\)-threshold.

**Equal-tail lemma.** Let \(f\) be a finite nonnegative concave function on
\([0,1]\), and let
\[
T=\int_0^1 f(x)\,dx.
\]
Suppose \(l,s\ge0\), \(l+s<1\), and
\[
\int_0^l f(x)\,dx
=
\int_{1-s}^1 f(x)\,dx
=A.
\tag{8}
\]
Then
\[
2A\le(l+s)T.
\tag{9}
\]

To prove this, assume first that \(l,s>0\), and put
\[
S=l+s,\qquad
\mathcal D=l(1-l)+s(1-s),
\]
\[
\lambda
=-\frac{(l-s)(1-S)}{\mathcal D},
\qquad
c
=S-\frac{(l-s)^2(1-S)}{\mathcal D}
=\frac{2ls(2-S)}{\mathcal D}.
\tag{10}
\]
In particular,
\[
0<c\le S.
\tag{11}
\]
Define the piecewise-constant weight
\[
W(x)=
\begin{cases}
1+\lambda-c,&0\le x\le l,\\
-c,&l<x<1-s,\\
1-\lambda-c,&1-s\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\tag{12}
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
\int_0^1W(x)\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_0^1xW(x)\,dx=0,
\tag{13}
\]
and
\[
1+\lambda-c
=\frac{2s(1-l)(1-S)}{\mathcal D}\ge0,
\]
\[
1-\lambda-c
=\frac{2l(1-s)(1-S)}{\mathcal D}\ge0.
\tag{14}
\]

Changing the two endpoint values of \(f\) to their one-sided limits does
not change any integral, so we may assume that \(f\) is continuous on the
closed interval.  This is automatic for section lengths of a planar convex
body.
Every nonnegative concave function has the distributional representation
\[
f(x)=(1-x)f(0)+xf(1)
+\int_0^1G_t(x)\,d\mu(t),
\tag{15}
\]
where \(\mu=-f''\) is a nonnegative measure and
\[
G_t(x)=\min\{x(1-t),\,t(1-x)\}.
\]
Piecewise-linear approximation proves (15) first for polygons and then for
every finite concave \(f\).

The two affine terms in (15) are annihilated by (13).  Put
\[
\Psi(t)=\int_0^1W(x)G_t(x)\,dx.
\]
Using (13), one may write
\[
\Psi(t)=\int_0^t(x-t)W(x)\,dx.
\tag{16}
\]
For \(0\le t\le l\), equations (14) and (16) give
\[
\Psi(t)
=-\frac{1+\lambda-c}{2}t^2\le0.
\tag{17}
\]
For \(1-s\le t\le1\), the equivalent right-tail formula gives
\[
\Psi(t)
=-\frac{1-\lambda-c}{2}(1-t)^2\le0.
\tag{18}
\]
On \([l,1-s]\), one has
\[
\Psi''(t)=c>0.
\]
Thus \(\Psi\) is convex there, so its maximum on that interval is attained
at an endpoint.  Equations (17)--(18) show that both endpoint values are
nonpositive.  Hence
\[
\Psi(t)\le0\quad(0\le t\le1).
\]
Equations (13), (15), and \(\mu\ge0\) now imply
\[
\int_0^1W(x)f(x)\,dx\le0.
\]
Using the equalities in (8), this is
\[
(1+\lambda)A+(1-\lambda)A-cT
=2A-cT\le0.
\]
Together with \(c\le S\), this proves (9).  If \(l=0\) or \(s=0\), then
(8) and concavity give \(A=0\), and (9) follows by a limit.  The
equal-tail lemma is proved.

We now pass to the needle.  The point limit is immediate.  Each boundary
in (2) must approach the limiting point, because both sides have positive
relative \(E_n\)-area by (4)--(5).  If the point is \(z_*\), then
\[
h_{i,n}\longrightarrow-\ell_i(z_*),
\qquad
\sum_i h_{i,n}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The first inclusion in (6) places \(P_n\) in a triangle whose linear scale
is \(\sum_i h_{i,n}\).  Its area therefore tends to zero.  Hence (7) holds
in the point case.

Suppose the Hausdorff limit is a nondegenerate segment \(J\).  Restrict the
three affine functions in (2) to \(J\).  A nonconstant restriction cuts a
left or right tail.  Three positive tails cannot be pairwise disjoint:
two have the same orientation, and their intersection has positive
one-dimensional measure.  The zero areas of all double-failure \(Q\)-cells
therefore force one restriction to be constant.  Two restrictions cannot
be constant, because the kernels of two distinct \(\ell_i\) have no common
nonzero direction.  After relabeling, the first and second boundaries cut
the left and right tails, while the third boundary is parallel to \(J\)
and survives only in the transverse blow-up.

Parametrize \(J\) by \(t\in[0,1]\).  Let \(l\) and \(s\) be the limiting
left and right tail widths.  Intersect \(E_n\) with the good side
\(Q_{3,n}\) before taking sections.  This is a convex body.  By (4)--(5),
its relative area is
\[
\frac7{12}+\frac5{36}+\frac5{36}
=\frac{31}{36},
\tag{19}
\]
and its left and right tails have relative areas \(5/36\) each.  Its
section-length function along \(J\) is nonnegative and concave, including
zero endpoint sections.  Apply the equal-tail lemma with
\[
T=\frac{31}{36},\qquad A=\frac5{36}.
\]
It gives the exact projection constraint
\[
S:=l+s\ge\frac{2A}{T}=\frac{10}{31}.
\tag{20}
\]
This is the step lost if one first replaces the whole \(A_2\)-density by
zero.

Choose the orientation so that, along \(J\),
\[
\ell_1(t)=a+\gamma t,\qquad
\ell_2(t)=b-\gamma t,\qquad
\ell_3(t)=c,
\tag{21}
\]
where \(\gamma>0\) and \(a+b+c=0\).  The first \(Q\)-threshold lies at
\(t=l\), the second lies at \(t=1-s\), and the transverse third threshold
has vanishing unscaled displacement from \(J\).  Therefore
\[
h_1=-a-\gamma l,\qquad
h_2=-b+\gamma-\gamma s,\qquad
h_3=-c
\tag{22}
\]
in the needle limit, and
\[
H:=h_1+h_2+h_3=\gamma(1-S).
\tag{23}
\]

For \(z\in P_n\), set
\[
x_i=h_{i,n}-\ell_i(z).
\]
The first inclusion in (6) gives \(x_i\ge0\), while
\(\sum_i\ell_i=0\) gives
\[
x_1+x_2+x_3\longrightarrow H.
\tag{24}
\]
Midpoint containment in (6) implies, for every \(i\),
\[
\ell_i(z)+\min_{w\in E_n}\ell_i(w)\ge-2.
\tag{25}
\]
The cap depths from the support endpoints to the first two thresholds are
\(\gamma l\) and \(\gamma s\).  The third depth tends to zero.  Combining
(22) and (25) yields the limiting box constraints
\[
0\le x_1\le2-\gamma l,\qquad
0\le x_2\le2-\gamma s,\qquad
0\le x_3\le2,
\tag{26}
\]
together with \(x_1+x_2+x_3=H\).

It remains to compute the largest possible area of (26).  We record the
calculation separately.  Put
\[
r=\frac{1-S}{S},\qquad d=\gamma S,\qquad
b=r+\frac12.
\]
Then \(H=rd\), while the first two box widths have sum \(4-d\).  Drop the
constraint \(x_3\le2\), which can only enlarge the section.  For fixed
\(d\), the resulting section is largest when the first two widths are
equal:
\[
w_1=w_2=w=2-\frac d2.
\tag{27}
\]
Indeed, if \(H\) is below both widths there is nothing to prove; if it
crosses one or both widths, the exact inclusion-exclusion formula is
\[
H^2-(H-w_1)_+^2-(H-w_2)_+^2
+(H-w_1-w_2)_+^2,
\]
and equalizing \(w_1,w_2\) increases this expression.  In the last regime
\(H\ge w_1+w_2\), it equals \(2w_1w_2\), which is again maximized by
equality.

With (27), the enlarged section-area numerator, relative to the simplex
of scale \(H\), is
\[
F(d)=
\begin{cases}
H^2,&H\le w,\\
H^2-2(H-w)^2,&w\le H\le2w,\\
2w^2,&H\ge2w.
\end{cases}
\tag{28}
\]
In the first regime, \(bd\le2\), so
\[
F(d)\le\frac{4r^2}{b^2}
\le\frac{8r^2}{2b^2-r^2}.
\tag{29}
\]
In the middle regime,
\[
F(d)=r^2d^2-2(bd-2)^2
\le\frac{8r^2}{2b^2-r^2},
\tag{30}
\]
where the right side is the exact maximum of the concave quadratic.
In the last regime, \(d(r+1)\ge4\).  Since \(w\) decreases with \(d\),
\[
F(d)\le8(1-S)^2
\le\frac{8r^2}{2b^2-r^2}.
\tag{31}
\]
The last comparison follows from
\[
2b^2-r^2=\frac{1-S^2/2}{S^2}.
\]

The coordinate simplex
\[
\{y_i\ge0,\ y_1+y_2+y_3=3\}
\]
is exactly \(K\) under \(y_i=\ell_i+1\).  Areas therefore scale by the
square of the simplex scale, and (28)--(31) give
\[
\frac{\limsup |P_n|}{|K|}
\le
\frac{8(1-S)^2}{9(1-S^2/2)}.
\tag{32}
\]
The right side is strictly decreasing for \(0<S<1\).  Substitution of
(20) gives
\[
\frac{\limsup |P_n|}{|K|}
\le
\frac{
8(21/31)^2
}{
9\left(1-\frac12(10/31)^2\right)
}
=\frac{392}{911}.
\tag{33}
\]
Finally,
\[
\frac{392}{911}<\frac49
\]
because \(9\cdot392=3528<3644=4\cdot911\).  This proves (7).

The use of the third good halfspace in (19) is essential.  If one keeps
only the total vanishing \(A_2\)-density, the equal-tail mass is
\(5/36\) relative to total mass one and only gives
\(l+s\ge5/18\), which is too weak for the proposed \(4/9\) bound.  The
convex \(31/36\)-mass good part is exactly the transverse information
carried by the four-cell ratios (4)--(5).
statement:
Let \(\ell_1,\ell_2,\ell_3\) be nonzero linear forms on
\(\mathbb R^2\), with distinct kernels and
\[
\ell_1+\ell_2+\ell_3=0.
\]
Put
\[
K=\{z:\ell_i(z)\ge-1,\ i=1,2,3\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus \(K\) is the centroidal triangle in the equality classification of
accepted facts `22d750674c663f88` and `e1361027c1dda6fa`.

For each \(n\), let \(E_n\) be a two-dimensional convex body and let
\(h_{1,n},h_{2,n},h_{3,n}\in\mathbb R\).  Use the three \(Q\)-halfspaces
\[
Q_{i,n}=\{\ell_i\ge-h_{i,n}\}
\tag{2}
\]
and their reflected \(P\)-halfspaces
\[
P_{i,n}=\{\ell_i\ge h_{i,n}\}.
\tag{3}
\]
Assume that the only positive exact \(Q\)-cells of \(E_n\) have relative
areas
\[
\frac{|E_n\cap Q_{1,n}\cap Q_{2,n}\cap Q_{3,n}|}{|E_n|}
=\frac7{12},
\tag{4}
\]
\[
\frac{|E_n\cap Q_{j,n}\cap Q_{k,n}\setminus Q_{i,n}|}{|E_n|}
=\frac5{36}
\quad(i=1,2,3),
\tag{5}
\]
and every other exact \(Q\)-cell has area zero.

Let \(P_n\) be a convex body satisfying
\[
P_n\subseteq\{\ell_i\le h_{i,n},\ i=1,2,3\},
\qquad
\frac{P_n+E_n}{2}\subseteq K.
\tag{6}
\]
Suppose that \(E_n\) converges in Hausdorff distance to a point or a
segment.  In the segment case, assume the standard transverse needle
limit: after parametrizing the limiting segment by \(t\in[0,1]\) and
rescaling perpendicular to it, the three \(Q\)-boundaries and the exact
cells in (4)--(5) converge.  This includes arbitrary concave transverse
widths, a slanted limiting third boundary, zero endpoint widths, and
threshold contacts on support faces.

Then
\[
\boxed{\qquad
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{|P_n|}{|K|}
\le\frac{392}{911}<\frac49.
\qquad}
\tag{7}
\]
In particular, a transverse needle limit cannot coexist with the escape
balance
\[
\frac{|P_{\varnothing,n}|}{|K_n|}\longrightarrow1
\]
in the centroidal-triangle middle limit.
